claims.text: Model health check status is ok with a window recall of 0.987261, reference recall of 0.98308, 471 illicit transactions in window, and a lag of 2.

The transaction matched a chain structural pattern indicating sequential transfers through a chain of intermediary accounts and layering of funds, with a chain length of 4, 1469 flagged instances, an observed illicit rate of 0.257318, a baseline illicit rate of 0.115809, and a lift of 2.221913.

The subgraph summary shows a radius of 2, 5 nodes, 4 edges, a density of 0.2, a focal in-degree of 1, a focal out-degree of 1, a max in-degree of 1, a max out-degree of 1, 0 alerted nodes, a share alerted of 0.0, a focal chain length of 4, and a wcc size of 5507.
Features f53 and f59 pushed the score up; features f131, f18, and f132 pushed the score down.

background.paraphrase: FATF guidance lists red flag indicators involving multiple layering of fiat funds and transfers across multiple accounts before virtual asset purchases.
background.quote: In various instances, the individuals shared the same resid ential address; and most of the VA addresses were accessed from the same IP address – indicating the potential use of money mules by professional money launderers to launder the illicit proceeds. In addition, multiple layering of the fiat funds was arranged prior to the VA purchase by mules.

background.paraphrase: FinCEN guidance highlights indicators such as an unusually complex series of transactions indicative of layering activity involving multiple accounts, banks, parties, and jurisdictions.
background.quote: • a lack of evidence of legitimate business activity, or any business operations at all, undertaken by many of the parties to the transaction(s); • unusual financial nexuses and transactions occurring among certain business types (e.g., food importer dealing with an auto parts exporter); • transactions that are not commensurate with the stated business type and/or that are unusual and unexpected in comparison with the volumes of similar businesses operating in the same locale; • unusually large numbers and/or volumes of wire transfers and/or repetitive wire transfer patterns; • unusually complex series of transactions indicative of layering activity involving multiple accounts, banks, parties, jurisdictions;

limitations: The Elliptic dataset has no wallet addresses, names, amounts or dates, so none of these appear in this memo.
The model's recall collapsed after time step 43 (a dark-market shutdown), and the model-health check only detects such a collapse several steps later, so scores at later time steps may be unreliable.
Regulation retrieval is weak (hybrid hit@3 about 0.6 on a small test set): retrieved passages are leads for an analyst, not verified authorities, and text from the India document comes from OCR.
Scores are raw gradient-boosting outputs, not calibrated probabilities; the calibrated value shifts with the prevalence of illicit activity.
Structural patterns are resemblances only: Elliptic has no typology labels.
The model-health monitor uses labels with a 2-step lag and a 3-step window, so it cannot flag a collapse in its first steps. On this dataset it first flags at step 47.
This is a draft for a human analyst. It does not decide whether a report should be filed.
